tasks.short: Supervise employees at the geothermal plant and in the well fields.

steps.what: Read which employees are rostered at the geothermal plant and well fields
Meet those employees on the plant and in the well fields
Give those employees the jobs for this shift
Stop employees when their work is unsafe
Answer questions employees bring during the shift

tasks.design: She still meets employees at the geothermal plant and in the well fields, gives the shift jobs, and stops unsafe work. The roster in the {HCM} only shows who should be there. Nothing is added that scores or directs an employee.
tasks.previous_blocker: The unsafe act and the person doing it are in front of her. A roster screen does not show either.
tasks.enabler_now: The shift roster was already on a screen. No new tool removes the need to stand with the crew.
tasks.still_hard: She has to see the work and the person. A name on a roster is not supervision.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which employee can take a harder job on this shift, and when to stop a job that still looks routine.
tasks.altitude: Her week on the floor is the same. She still gives the jobs and stops unsafe work. No decision right moves.

reach.task: Correct unsafe work on a live line without taking the job off the operator.
reach.learn: Which stops the operator is already allowed to make alone.

evidence.claim: Watching employees and stopping unsafe work on a live plant is not replaced by reading a roster.
GDPR article 22 bars a significant decision about a person made solely by automation.
WOR article 27 requires works-council consent for staff-data processing and for staff monitoring, unless a collective agreement settles it.

assumptions: The focal role is the geothermal production manager. Operators are another role and are not in these shares.
Roster fields are employee name, shift start, shift end, and location (plant or well field). The planner writes them in the {HCM} before the shift. This task only reads them.
If the roster is late, she asks the crew who is here. That fallback is already how the shift starts, and it stays.
No map, score, or template is added. Existing roster runtime is not her hours.
unknowns: Whether she or a planner writes the roster at this plant.
research_questions: How often is the roster wrong when she reaches the well fields?

already_counted.description: Time on the plant and in the well fields stays in s2.

incremental.description: No template or map to keep. The planner maintains the roster.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Nothing in supervising employees changes. A roster on screen does not shorten the time she stands with them in the well fields. Low and high are 0.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Oversee repairs and operations so the plant meets the standards.

steps.what: Read the geothermal plant state and the open repairs
Read the standards that govern those repairs
Scan repair records for inspections past the due date
Compare the repairs on site with those standards
Decide if the plant stays online under those standards

tasks.design: Technicians already enter a due date and a completion on the repair record in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A configured list shows inspections whose due date is before today and whose completion is empty. She still reads the standards, walks the repairs, and decides whether the plant stays online. The list is not a staff score, and she does not file it anywhere else.
tasks.previous_blocker: Late inspections sat inside a long repair list. Finding them meant scrolling, so it waited for a quieter read.
tasks.enabler_now: The due date and the completion are already fields on the repair record when the technician fills them. Showing the late ones is a filter, not a new record.
tasks.still_hard: A permit can stop a restart even when every inspection date is current. She judges that on site, next to the repair.
tasks.human_edge: She knows when a standard is met on the record and the repair is still unsafe to leave running.

ambition.what: Whether a late inspection stops the plant on the day the due date passes, not at the monthly read of the repair list.

tasks.altitude: She still decides whether the plant stays online. The late inspection is visible the day it is late, and the walk and the standards stay hers.

reach.task: Decide which repairs must finish before a unit returns to service.
reach.learn: Which permit points stop a restart even when the inspection dates are current.

evidence.claim: A repair record that stores a due date and a completion date can be filtered to due dates before today with an empty completion. That filter is configuration, not a model.
WOR article 27 requires works-council consent for staff-data processing and for staff monitoring, unless a collective agreement settles it.

assumptions: The focal role is the geothermal production manager. Maintenance technicians are another role and are not in these shares.

Repair-record fields used by the filter are equipment id, inspection due date, completion date, and status. The maintenance technician enters the due date when the job is planned and the completion when the job is finished, in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
If the due date is blank, that inspection stays off the late list and she still finds it while reading the open repairs in s1. No separate map of inspection types is kept by her.
The run or stop call is spoken to the plant operator on site. It is not a filing to an authority and it is not a second save of the repair record.
Works-council consent is in the build because a staff-monitoring reading of the same list would need it. This list does not name who did the inspection.
unknowns: Whether this plant's repair records already store a due date and a completion date.
What share of inspections have the due date filled in.
research_questions: How long does she spend scrolling the repair list for late inspections on a normal day?

already_counted.description: Deciding if the plant stays online stays in s5, after she has walked the repair.

incremental.description: No map or template to keep. Technicians enter the due date. She does not maintain inspection codes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the scroll for inspections past their due date is removed, and only where the technician already entered that date. Low 3: about a third of records have a date, so most of the scroll remains inside s1. High 8: dates are usually filled, while the walk and the keep-running decision stay. High is under the 10 point net because blank dates are still her look-up.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Tell employees the geothermal plant conditions they must know.

steps.what: Read geothermal plant conditions in the night log and on the screens
Choose the conditions employees must hear
Copy those chosen readings into the handover note
Tell employees the plant conditions at handover
Answer employees who radio from the wells about conditions

tasks.design: She still chooses which geothermal plant conditions employees must hear, and she still says them at handover and on the radio. A configured copy moves only the readings she marked from the {OPS_SYSTEM} into the handover note in the {DOCS}. It copies numbers. It does not write the warning, and she does not send the note outside the plant.
tasks.previous_blocker: The readings and the warning were written as one note, so the numbers were not a separate copy from the historian.
tasks.enabler_now: The historian already stores the readings. Marking the few that matter is enough for a field copy into the note.
tasks.still_hard: A copied reading does not tell someone to stay clear of a hot well. She has to say that, and she has to answer the radio.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which condition will change how this crew starts, and which reading would only worry them.
tasks.altitude: She still decides what employees hear and she still says it. She stops retyping readings she has already marked. The radio answers stay hers.

reach.task: Tell the incoming crew which plant conditions change how they start the shift.
reach.learn: Which few readings the crew must hear before they touch equipment.

evidence.claim: A plant historian already stores periodic readings. Copying a marked subset of those readings into a note is a field copy, not a drafted warning.
GDPR article 22 bars a significant decision about a person made solely by automation.

assumptions: The focal role is the geothermal production manager. Employees who hear the handover are another role and are not in these shares.
Copied fields are point id, value, unit, and time. Instruments write them to the historian in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. She selects which points in s2. The copy does not compose a sentence.
If a point is missing from the historian, she types that one reading herself. That is why the saved time stays below the whole copy step.
The spoken handover and the radio answer are talk with colleagues, not a versioned send. No wording template is maintained.
The handover note is this task's record of the numbers. It is not reused as a card or a line on other tasks.
unknowns: Whether she retypes readings today or only says them.
Which historian points the handover actually uses.
research_questions: How many readings does she retype into the handover note on a normal morning?

already_counted.description: Telling employees the conditions at handover stays in s4.

incremental.description: No warning template to keep. She chooses the conditions in s2. Instruments already store the readings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the retype of readings she has already chosen, from the historian into the handover note, is removed. Low 3: she retypes a few numbers and says the rest. High 7: most handover numbers are copied, and she still speaks every warning and still answers the radio. Missing points stay typed by her, so the high stays under the 9 point net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find inefficiencies in geothermal plant equipment and procedures.

steps.what: Identify odd trends in the geothermal plant systems
Record expected output after a test of that equipment
Calculate the gap from those trends to the expected output
Inspect equipment for leaks, fouling and short cycling
Evaluate which of those gaps are real inefficiencies
Write the procedural change or the repair for that gap

tasks.design: She still records the expected output after a performance test, still walks the equipment, and still decides which gap is a real inefficiency. A configured view subtracts that expected output from the historian trends in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. The workbook arithmetic goes away. She still writes the procedural change or the repair. The view does not score the crew.
tasks.previous_blocker: The expected output lived in a workbook beside an export. The historian did not hold the test result, so the subtraction was hand work.
tasks.enabler_now: Generation, steam and reinjection are already stored as numbers. The test result is a few numbers she already writes down. Subtraction does not need a model.
tasks.still_hard: Leaks, fouling and short cycling are on the equipment, not in the trend. A gap can be a bad test or a bad sensor, not an inefficiency.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell a well problem from weather and from a drifting sensor, which the subtraction cannot.

ambition.what: Whether an output gap on a normal weekday is worth a repair, not only in the week she runs a performance test.

tasks.altitude: She still decides which gap is worth a repair or a procedural change. On ordinary days the subtraction is already done, so that call does not wait for a workbook afternoon. The test result is still hers to enter.

reach.task: Turn a performance test into the expected output a later gap uses.
reach.learn: Which test points the gap calculation is allowed to use, and which stay a hand check.

evidence.claim: Subtracting a stored expected output from stored generation, steam and reinjection totals is arithmetic on fields the historian and the test record already hold.
WOR article 27 requires works-council consent for staff-data processing and for staff monitoring, unless a collective agreement settles it.

assumptions: The focal role is the geothermal production manager. Control staff who keep historian tags are another role and are not in these shares. Their tag upkeep is not a saving and is not charged to her.

Expected-output fields are equipment id, test date, expected generation, expected steam, and expected reinjection. She writes them in s2 from the performance test. Today that write is a workbook. The configured view reads those same fields.
Historian fields are generation, steam, and reinjection by hour, written by instruments. If a quantity is absent, that gap stays a workbook calculation and is not in the removed step.
She does not keep a second map of tags. Entering the test result is s2, already inside this task, not extra upkeep.
The procedural change is an internal note to maintenance. It is not sent to an authority, and it is not a save of the gap back onto the historian.
unknowns: Whether the historian at this plant stores reinjection as well as generation and steam.
How often she runs a performance test and writes the expected output.
research_questions: Which of the three quantities does she still calculate by hand because the historian does not store them?

already_counted.description: Evaluating which gaps are real inefficiencies stays in s5, using the site notes and the gap.

incremental.description: No tag map to keep. Expected output is entered in s2. Control staff maintain historian tags.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the workbook subtraction of historian trends from the expected output is removed. Low 5: the historian holds generation only, so steam and reinjection stay hand work inside the old arithmetic. High 11: all three quantities and the test result are present, while the walk, the evaluation, and the written change stay. A bad sensor still forces a hand check, so the high stays under the 15 point net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still supervises employees on the plant and in the well fields, still decides whether the plant stays online, still says the conditions the crew must hear, and still judges which gap is a real inefficiency. She spends less time scrolling for late inspections, retyping handover readings, and subtracting expected output in a workbook.
reach: Industrial Production Managers: which stops an operator may make alone, and which performance-test points a gap calculation may use.
Hydroelectric Production Managers: which permit points stop a restart when inspection dates are already current.
Biomass Power Plant Managers: which few readings the incoming crew must hear before they touch equipment.
skills_to_grow: Name the permit point that stops a restart.
Mark only the readings employees must hear.
Enter the expected output from a performance test as fields a later subtraction can read.
role.ambitious_version: On a normal weekday she sees the output gap for each well and calls a repair before the planned outage, while the crew still hears the conditions from her in person.
